name: Adobe InDesign
note: Every row of Adobe's InDesign keyboard-shortcuts page (helpx.adobe.com/indesign/using/default-keyboard-shortcuts.html now redirects to the desktop path). The context is the page's own table heading (Selection and navigation tools, Other tools, Selecting and moving objects, Character formatting, Kerning and tracking, Navigating and selecting text, Tables, Panels, Specific panels, XML, Separations Preview, ...). Adobe often prints several keys in one row - "Alt + Up/Down Arrow", "Ctrl + 5, 2, or 4", "Alt + Arrow key" - and a chord holds one key, so those rows become one action per key with the chord repeated in parentheses after Adobe's own wording. The pairing is deliberately not guessed: Adobe writes "Increase/decrease kerning and tracking | Alt + Left/Right Arrow" in an order that does not match how InDesign actually behaves, so no row here claims which half of a described behaviour belongs to which key. Mouse gestures are left out: everything in Color and swatches, three rows of Styles, four rows of Panels, all of Transforming objects except High Quality Display, and the tool-plus-modifier and drag rows of Selecting and moving objects, Tables and Viewing documents. "Start row on the next column" and "Start row on next frame" are left out because Adobe specifies the numeric-keypad Enter, which the chord grammar does not address. "Switch to the next/previous document window" is left out because its three Windows alternatives and three macOS alternatives are printed in different orders and cannot be paired safely. Adobe's "~" is written here as the ` key it sits on, and ">" / "<" as Shift+. and Shift+, . The Platform-specific variations table is macOS only, so those seven actions carry no Windows chord.
